observed_funding_interpretation: ETH perp funding currently negative (shorts pay longs); SHORT hedge is a cost, not income
decision_basis: D1 static model finds 6 cells with positive net_pnl_hedged under both 0% and +5% APR funding scenarios (sustainable edge under realistic funding). All 6 cells are on 0xb2cc (Aerodrome) with ±5% range, 24h hold, 75% hedge. Min viable capital is $250 with $0.05/day net (0.02% of size). Signal/noise at the best cells is 1.18-1.24, marginal. Current observed funding is -8% APR (shorts pay), which would wipe out the edge. The delta-hedge doesn't rescue the fee-only LP; it provides a thin edge under favorable assumptions.
il_formula_note: D1 replaces R4C's overstated IL formula (size × σ²/R² × 0.5 × hold_days, which gave $400/day IL on $50 ±1%) with a realistic LVR-based formula (LVR_daily = 0.5 × σ_daily², with range amplification capped at 5%/day). The D1 formula is appropriate for tight-range CLMM LPs and gives $0.04-$0.08/day IL on $50 size across the range grid.

why_D1_matters: D1 closes one of the three open questions from R4C: can a SHORT hedge rescue the fee-only LP? Answer: barely. The math says 6 cells with positive EV under realistic funding (0% to +5% APR), with min viable capital $250 and best net $0.68/day at $1000 ±5% 24h on 0xb2cc. The edge is thin (0.02-0.07% of size per day) and funding-dependent (current -8% APR wipes it out). The model is not a flat NO_GO, but it's not a GO either — it's NEED_MORE_DATA. The next stages (D2 dynamic-delta, D3 funding history, D4 pool expansion) would test whether the edge can be thickened.
